Report_ID: Death from cardiovascular disease (fatal myocardial infarction, fatal stroke, sudden death)
Title: The Antioxidant Acetylcysteine Reduces Cardiovascular Events in Patients With End-Stage Renal Failure: A Randomized, Controlled Trial
Author: Tepel M, van der Giet M, Statz M, Jankowski J, Zidek W
Comment: P value and CI reproduced verbatim from text ("P-0.80" is OCR for P=0.80). Trial was not blinded despite the placebo-controlled description.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Acetylcysteine group (600 mg BID orally)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Adults with end-stage renal failure on maintenance hemodialysis (>=3 months, 3x weekly)
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of patients dying from cardiovascular disease per randomised arm
Outcome variable: Death from cardiovascular disease (fatal myocardial infarction, fatal stroke, sudden death)
effect_direction: favours control (more CV deaths with acetylcysteine: 9/64 vs 8/70; RR 1.23)

Title: Effects of vitamin E on cardiovascular outcomes in people with mild-to-moderate renal insufficiency: Results of the HOPE Study
Author: Mann JFE, Lonn EM, Yi Q, Gerstein HC, Hoogwerf BJ, Pogue J, Bosch J, Dagenais GR, Yusuf S
Comment: Post-hoc subgroup of the HOPE trial (full trial N=9541); subgroup counts/denominators used as required. Table 2 footnote states 'A patient may have had more than one event' for this component row. The paper labels the effect 'RR, relative risk' in the Table 2 footnote, though the Results text describes the primary-outcome estimate as a hazard ratio from Cox regression.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Natural source vitamin E (RRR-alpha-tocopheryl acetate) 400 IU/day') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Country: Multinational (19 countries in North and South America and Europe)
Participant type: Adults aged >=55 years at high cardiovascular risk with mild-to-moderate renal insufficiency (serum creatinine 1.4-2.3 mg/dL)
Recruitment source: 267 participating centers in the HOPE trial
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of participants who died from cardiovascular causes
effect_direction: essentially null / marginally favours antioxidant (57/499 vs 57/494; RR 0.97)

Report_ID: Cardiovascular death (death due to myocardial infarction + death due to cerebrovascular accident)
Title: Selenium supplementation improves the nutritional status of hemodialysis patients: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
Author: Salehi M, Sohrabi Z, Ekramzadeh M, Fallahzadeh MK, Ayatollahi M, Geramizadeh B, Hassanzadeh J, Sagheb MM
Comment: No formal statistical test, p-value or effect measure reported for cardiovascular deaths. Events summed from the two cardiovascular fatal components (MI death + cerebrovascular accident death), which the paper itself labels "cardiovascular deaths" in the Discussion. Denominators are the randomized/ITT n=40 per arm, as the paper reports no separate adverse-event denominators.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Selenium group (selenium yeast 200 µg daily, 12 weeks)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-arm parallel trial
Participant type: Adults aged 18-80 years on maintenance hemodialysis for >=3 months, stable, without active infection
Recruitment source: Faghihi Hospital Hemodialysis Center, Shiraz, Iran (screened 280 patients, March-June 2009)
Outcome measurement: Number of patients with fatal serious adverse events of cardiovascular cause out of patients randomized per arm
Outcome variable: Cardiovascular death (death due to myocardial infarction + death due to cerebrovascular accident)
effect_direction: favours control (3/40 vs 2/40 CV deaths with selenium)

Title: Bardoxolone Methyl in Type 2 Diabetes and Stage 4 Chronic Kidney Disease
Author: de Zeeuw D, et al. (BEACON Trial Investigators)
Comment: Trial terminated early (median follow-up 9 months). 'Death from cardiovascular causes' was defined by the trial as death due to either cardiovascular or unknown causes. Figure 2B legend's 19 vs 13 refers to CV death as the FIRST event of the secondary composite, not the total CV death count; totals of 27 vs 19 were used. Hazard ratio adjusted for baseline eGFR and urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Bardoxolone methyl 20 mg daily') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: nephrology / cardiovascular outcomes in chronic kidney disease
Country: Multinational (United States, European Union, Australia, Canada, Israel, Mexico)
Participant type: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and stage 4 chronic kidney disease (eGFR 15 to <30 ml/min/1.73 m2)
Recruitment source: Multicenter clinical trial sites, June 2011 through September 2012
Outcome measurement: Number of patients who died from cardiovascular causes out of number randomized per arm

Title: Secondary prevention with antioxidants of cardiovascular disease in endstage renal disease (SPACE): randomised placebo-controlled trial
Author: Boaz M, et al.
Comment: Paper notes 23 CVD deaths in text while table counts sum to 24 (9+15); counts from Table 2/Table 3 used as reported. Text also reports a Kaplan-Meier p=0.06 and Cox smoking-adjusted p=0.1 for CVD mortality; the crude relative risk is extracted per plan.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Vitamin E 800 IU/day') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Chronic haemodialysis patients aged 40-75 years with pre-existing cardiovascular disease
Recruitment source: Six haemodialysis centres in greater Tel Aviv, Israel
Outcome measurement: Number of participants dying of cardiovascular disease out of number randomised per arm
